newsitem.title: EGYPT: Sugar - Egypt develops production from beet.
newsitem.headline: Sugar - Egypt develops production from beet.

text.p: Egypt is developing its production of sugar extracted from beet and aims to gradually decrease its imports of raw sugar, industry sources said.

Mohamed Safwat Seiam, head of sales and export at the government Sugar and Integrated Industries Co (SIIC), said Egypt had already committed itself to importing 800,000 tonnes of raw sugar in 1997, but imports in 1998 were expected to be at the most 600,000 tonnes.
"Maybe less than this quantity because we are starting beet sugar refining," he said on Wednesday.
Industry sources said Egypt's output of beet sugar would start rising from 1998, when it added to refining capacity, and would reach at least 360,000 tonnes in about three years.
Egypt's only beet sugar refinery, Delta Sugar Co, now produced between 100,000 and 120,000 tonnes of fine grain white sugar from beets, Delta's agricultural engineer Osman Attia said on Thursday.
In 1998, it would start up a second line and production could double gradually over the next three years, he said.
At the same time a new beet sugar refinery, Dakahlia, was due to start refining and was expected to produce between 100,000 and 120,000 tonnes a year, industry sources said.
Seiam said Dakahlia trial production would start before June.

There were also plans to set up a fourth line. Egyptian investors agreed in November to set up the Fayoum Sugar Co beet sugar plant with a paid-up capital of 200 million pounds ($59 million). Its planned output was 120,000 tonnes a year.
Industry sources said beet cultivation in Egypt to supply the Dakahlia and Delta plants was about 10,000 acres and 50,000 acres respectively this year.
Attia said Delta planned to expand the cultivated beet area by about 20,000 acres in 1998 to meet expanded output.
He said in three years, total Delta beet acreage under cultivation would be about 100,000 acres if the yield was 18 tonnes per acre, and less if the yield was 20 tonnes per acre.

Delta consultant Ahmed Zohdy said the company produced beet pulp pellets and molasses for export. Its white sugar was used for local consumption, but Zohdy said if the price was right on international markets Delta could consider exports.
"In two or three years Egypt could be nearer to self-sufficiency in sugar, depending upon the increase in the size of the population," he said. "At least there will be a smaller gap."
Egypt's total annual sugar consumption is 1.65 million tonnes, SIIC media adviser Mohammed Amin said on Wednesday.
Egypt's cane sugar output in the 1996/97 production season should reach 1.009 million tonnes in terms of white sugar value, German statistician F.O. Licht said in a report last year.
Amin has put Egypt's total beet and cane sugar output at some 1.2 million tonnes in the last production season.
